Brand Identity System Composed In One Mark

nodes.label: Fireworks Star Emblem
nodes.rationale: Five-pointed star with a double gold/blue outline framing a real fireworks explosion photo on black. It is the only element that states the product category outright, so it carries the storefront's merchandising promise (pyrotechnics) where the letterform cannot. A raster photo inside an otherwise vector-looking star means the emblem degrades at favicon sizes.

nodes.label: Gold Orbital Ring Motif
nodes.rationale: A gold ellipse drawn in false perspective, passing behind the P at the top and in front of it at the bottom. Its job is compositional: it binds the letterform and the star into one silhouette and supplies the accent color, but it also forces the logo into a wide landscape bounding box with large empty corners, which constrains navbar height and horizontal alignment.

nodes.label: Blue P Monogram
nodes.rationale: Oversized slanted blue letter P acting as the brand initial. Its counter (the bowl's hole) is partly occluded by the star, so the letter is only cleanly readable at larger sizes; the monogram is the brand-name carrier while the star is the category carrier.

nodes.label: NavBar Brand Logo Mark
nodes.rationale: Transparent-background PNG logo consumed by the NavBar Logo component. Composite identity mark: a large blue stylized letter P, a gold elliptical orbit sweeping behind and across it, and a red-and-gold five-pointed star containing a photographic fireworks burst at the optical center. Transparency and a horizontal 3:2 aspect let it drop into a light or dark navbar without a plate, which matters because the project added a dark mode (commit 'modo oscuro y buscador'). The gold/blue pair is the de facto brand palette the rest of the UI inherits.

nodes.label: Pyrotechnics Rebrand
nodes.rationale: The asset is named lavadora.png (Spanish for 'washing machine') and lives under a repo named lavadero-ecommerce ('laundromat'), yet the artwork contains no laundry imagery at all and depicts fireworks instead. The project was pivoted from a laundry storefront to a fireworks storefront (commit 'Cambio a fuegos artificiales') and only the artwork was swapped; the filename, directory and repo name were left on the old domain to avoid touching every import path. Consequence: asset names are no longer a reliable guide to asset content, and any search for brand assets by domain keyword will miss this file.

nodes.label: src/main.jsx Module Entry
nodes.rationale: Loaded as a native ES module from an unbundled /src path, which is the Vite dev-server convention rather than Create React App; the bundler rewrites this path at build time.

nodes.label: Favicon /lavadora.ico
nodes.rationale: Washing-machine icon left over from the original lavadero (laundry/car-wash) concept, and declared with an SVG MIME type while the file is named .ico, a mismatch browsers may refuse.

nodes.label: Shell lang=en on Spanish Storefront
nodes.rationale: The shell declares English while the title, documentation and UI copy are Spanish, an untouched scaffold default that misinforms screen readers and translation heuristics.

nodes.label: Document Title: Fuegos Artificiales
nodes.rationale: The storefront is branded as a fireworks shop. A single static title serves every route, so the tab label never reflects the product or category being viewed.

nodes.label: Carrito de Compras
nodes.rationale: Cart state is global via Context API instead of prop drilling or an external store (Redux/Zustand), keeping the dependency surface small while letting any route read the cart.

nodes.label: Catalogo de Productos
nodes.rationale: Items render dynamically from Firestore rather than from a bundled static list, so the catalog can change without a redeploy.

nodes.label: Checkout
nodes.rationale: The order id is generated by Firebase on document creation rather than by the client, so the backend owns uniqueness and the confirmation screen simply echoes the returned id.

nodes.label: Detalle de Producto
nodes.rationale: Stock is enforced at the detail view through a quantity counter, pushing the stock ceiling to the point of add-to-cart rather than validating it later at checkout.

nodes.label: Filtrado por Categoria
nodes.rationale: Filtering is expressed as category ROUTES instead of local component state, which makes a filtered view linkable, shareable and back-button friendly at the cost of a navigation round trip.

nodes.label: Firebase
nodes.rationale: Used as a realtime backend-as-a-service so the project ships with no custom API layer; products, purchase orders and contact messages all live in the same hosted store.

nodes.label: Firestore Database
nodes.rationale: Document/collection store acting as the single source of truth for items, orders and messages; its collections are the shared data contract between otherwise unconnected features.

nodes.label: Formulario de Contacto
nodes.rationale: Messages are written straight to the database instead of through an email/SMTP service, which removes any server-side dependency but means nobody is notified unless the database is inspected.

nodes.label: React Router Dom
nodes.rationale: Client-side routing is what makes category filtering and product detail addressable URLs inside a single-page app shell.

nodes.label: React Spinners
nodes.rationale: Added specifically to cover the async gap of Firestore fetches: because data arrives after first paint, every data-backed view needs a visible loading state.

nodes.label: Ecommerce React - Proyecto Final
nodes.rationale: Framed as a React final project: Firebase is chosen as a realtime backend so the project needs no custom server, and the feature set is the canonical ecommerce rubric (catalog, filter, detail, cart, checkout, contact).

nodes.label: Instalacion y Configuracion Local
nodes.rationale: Setup instructions are truncated after the clone step: no dependency install, no dev-server command and no Firebase credential/config step, so the documented procedure cannot produce a running app.

nodes.label: Domain Pivot: Lavadero to Fuegos Artificiales
nodes.norm_label: domain pivot: lavadero to fuegos artificiales
nodes.rationale: The project was retargeted from a laundry/car-wash business to a fireworks store, but the rebrand was partial: the repository directory and the favicon asset still carry the lavadero identity while the page title carries the new one. The generic ecommerce architecture (Firestore items plus categories) made the pivot cheap, which is likely why only surface strings were changed.

nodes.label: Single Page App HTML Shell
nodes.rationale: The served HTML is an empty shell: no server-rendered markup, one mount point, one ES-module script. Everything (routing, catalog, cart) is built client-side, which is why category filtering can be routes without any server route config, but also why the page has no crawlable content or per-route metadata.

nodes.label: Context API Global State
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the global-state mechanism for the cart because it is built into React: no extra library, no store boilerplate. Trade-off accepted: every consumer re-renders on any cart change, acceptable at this catalog size.
